title: Unit tests for an ad campaign budget pacer
name: Budget pacer tests

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how these unit tests are designed to check the pacer's decisions? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
At 12:00 UTC with a 1,000,000-micro daily budget and default tolerance, what is the largest spentTodayMicros that still gets reason "ok" (with a small bid that does not exhaust the budget)?
Why do the tests build times with explicit "Z" (UTC) ISO strings rather than local times?
choices: fractionOfDayElapsed uses getUTC* methods, so local-time inputs would give different fractions on machines in different timezones
Date cannot parse ISO strings without a timezone
It makes the tests run faster

questions.prompt: Near the end of the day (23:59 UTC), spend is 999,500 and the bid is 1,000. Which check decides the outcome?
choices: Neither; the bid is allowed because the day is almost over
The tolerance check, which is skipped near midnight
The exhaustion check, returning exhausted, because it runs first
